items.stem: The treasurer says, "Keep the booth cheap." The team spends 4,200 pesos on a banner and then cannot afford tables. Which part of the framing was missing?

options.text: A limit written as a number, such as a total of 5,000 pesos.
options.feedback: "Cheap" gave no number, so each person picked a different ceiling. With a total of 5,000 pesos, a 4,200-peso banner would have raised a flag at once.

options.text: A longer list of volunteers to share the work.
options.feedback: More volunteers do not say how much money each item may use. The overspending came from the missing number.

options.text: A larger booth with room for more tables.
options.feedback: A larger booth costs more, and the team would still not know its ceiling.

items.stem: One team writes the goal "A good turnout." Another writes "At least 80 visitors sign the sheet." At 5 PM the sheet has 62 names. What can each team say?

options.text: Both teams missed, since turnout cannot be measured at all.
options.feedback: Turnout can be measured by counting names. The first goal never named a count.

options.text: The second team missed by 18 names. The first team can argue either way.
options.feedback: 80 minus 62 is 18. The first goal has no count, so its result is open to debate.

options.text: Both teams succeeded, because 62 visitors is a fair crowd.
options.feedback: The second goal sets 80 as the line, so 62 misses it.

items.stem: A developer is asked to "build a sign-up page." The page works, but the org wanted every name copied into a shared spreadsheet. Which part of the problem was left out?

options.text: The input: which fields visitors fill in.
options.feedback: The page collected names, so the input was clear. The gap came after the form was submitted.

options.text: The limit: how fast the page loads.
options.feedback: Nobody asked about speed. The missing piece is what happens to the names.

options.text: The output: what must be produced and where it ends up.
options.feedback: The spreadsheet was the real output, and nobody wrote it down. The page produced a result nobody wanted.

items.stem: Two teammates plan the booth layout. One assumes there is a power outlet and the other assumes there is none. What should the team do first?

options.text: Plan for no outlet and skip the question.
options.feedback: This avoids one risk but may waste a laptop demo that would have worked.

options.text: Ask the organizers and write down the answer.
options.feedback: The organizers know the fact, and one message settles it. The plan then rests on a checked fact.

options.text: Vote on which assumption is likelier.
options.feedback: A vote counts opinions. The organizers have the answer.
